summary: The study investigates the structural evolution of HfO2 thin films deposited by atomic layer deposition (ALD) and annealed at varying temperatures. The films are analyzed using grazing incidence X-ray diffraction (GIXRD) and X-ray reflectivity (XRR) to evaluate their thickness, surface roughness, and crystallinity. The results show that the films remain stable with minimal roughness and that crystallinity evolves from an amorphous structure to polycrystalline monoclinic HfO2 upon high-temperature annealing.
evidence: HfO films were deposited on 100-mm (001 ) silicon wafers by ALD at ASM Microchemistry in a F-450 reactor using alternating surface saturating reactions between hafnium tetrachloride (HfCl4) and water at 300¯8C. Rapid thermal annealing (RTA) was performed in a JetFirst (Jipelec, France ) for 30 s in N at temperatures ranging between 300 and 1050 8C.
